texts.facts: The captioned petition is filed by the accused Nos. 1 to 6 seeking quashing of the proceedings pending in C.C.No.888/2024 for the offences punishable under Sections 143, 147, 323, 354, 504, 506 read with Section 149 of IPC arising out of Crime No.130/2024 of Manvi Police Station. 2. The gist of the prosecution case, as could be gathered from the complaint and charge sheet materials, is that the complainant is employed as a cook in a hotel and her husband one Mohd. Shafi was a lorry driver. The couple had six children. It is alleged that since the complainant's husband was obese, accused Nos.1 and 2-- Ambika and Kalyani respectively advised the complainant to persuade her husband to consume certain health- NC: 2025:KHC-K:7448 HC-KAR oriented nutrition products marketed by Herbalife Nutrition Company. 3. The complainant, acting on this advice, suggested to her husband to try the said herbal products. Although the complainant's husband is stated to have initially shown reluctance, accused Nos.1 to 3 allegedly prevailed upon the complainant and her husband by representing that several consumers had derived substantial health benefits from the use of such products. 4. It is further alleged that believing the assurances of accused Nos.1 to 3, the complainant and her husband attended a demonstration of the products and thereafter purchased items worth Rs.7,000/-. The deceased thereafter consumed the said products for one month, reportedly resulting in a weight loss of 4 kilograms. According to the complainant, accused No.3 again compelled the husband of the complainant to purchase a fresh set of herbal products for the subsequent NC: 2025:KHC-K:7448 HC-KAR month. It is alleged that upon continued consumption, the deceased began experiencing stomach pain, back pain, and giddiness. As his symptoms aggravated, the complainant claims to have taken her husband to various doctors for treatment. Ultimately, when they visited the Raichur Institute of Medical Sciences, they were informed that the deceased had suffered complete renal failure. 5. The complaint further narrates that on 16.05.2024 at about 1:00 p.m., the complainant, her husband, and two other persons, Javed Khan and Ajmat Khan, went to the footwear shop of accused No.3 located at Basaveshwar Complex, Manvi, and confronted the accused stating that the herbal products supplied by them had allegedly caused kidney failure in the complainant's husband. It is Ambika vs The State Of Karnataka on 3 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/11206542/ 3 alleged that at this juncture, accused Nos.1 to 6 formed an unlawful assembly. Accused Nos.2 and 3 are alleged to have attempted to outrage the modesty of the complainant, while accused No.4/Prema Bai allegedly assaulted her with hands. When Javed Khan and Ajmat NC: 2025:KHC-K:7448 HC-KAR Khan intervened, accused Nos.5 and 6 allegedly assaulted them as well. It is further alleged that all accused persons hurled filthy abuses at the complainant and her husband and threatened them with dire consequences. Based on these allegations, Crime No.130/2024 was registered for offences under Sections 143, 147, 323, 354, 504, 506 read with Section 149 of IPC. 6.
texts.arguments: Learned counsel for the petitioners, reiterating the grounds urged in the petition, contends that the continuation of criminal proceedings against the petitioners would amount to abuse of the process of law. He draws attention to the test reports obtained by the Investigating Officer which form part of the charge sheet and submits that the herbal products in question satisfy the standards prescribed for "Energy Drinks Mixed Powder" under the Food Safety and Standards (Food Products Standards and Food Additives) Regulations, 2011. The reports, according to him, clearly establish that the products are not harmful. NC: 2025:KHC-K:7448 HC-KAR 7. He further refers to the OPD records of the Raichur Institute of Medical Sciences relating to the deceased and submits that the deceased was a chronic alcoholic and smoker. By placing reliance on these medical records, counsel would submit that the complainant, out of frustration caused by her husband's medical condition, has attempted to rope in the petitioners though the renal failure was clearly attributable to the deceased's lifestyle vices. He thus submits that even if the charge sheet materials are accepted in totality, no offence is made out against the petitioners and therefore, the proceedings deserve to be [LEAKAGE_MASK]. 8. Per contra, learned High Court Government Pleader, placing reliance on the complaint and statements collected during investigation, contends that there are credible allegations that the petitioners assaulted the complainant, abused her, and attempted to outrage her modesty. Therefore, according to him, the matter requires NC: 2025:KHC-K:7448 HC-KAR to proceed to trial and no interference is warranted at this stage. 9.
